q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the headquarters of a zonal railway, the stores organisation is headed by the Controller of Stores.
2. At the divisional level, the stores organisation of a zonal railway is headed by the Senior Divisional Materials Manager.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Controller of Stores heads the stores organisation at zonal headquarters, and the Senior Divisional Materials Manager heads it at divisional level.

q: A finance officer vetting the Stores Budget of a railway finds that the anticipated issues of stores to revenue (working expense) heads have been linked with Primary Unit 32. The Primary Unit with which such issues to revenue heads are correctly linked is:
e: Anticipated issues of stores to revenue working expenses are linked with Primary Unit 27 in the Stores Budget, which classifies stores debits and credits by the head and unit they serve.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Stores Budget of a railway:
1. It is called a 'derived' budget because the stores requirements in it are derived from the works and maintenance programmes of the consuming departments.
2. It is prepared by the Railway Board directly, without reference to the programmes of the consuming departments.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 only is correct: the Stores Budget is a derived budget because stores requirements are derived from the works and maintenance programmes of consuming departments, not prepared independently by the Board.

q: At the close of the year, an accounts officer has to trace the statement showing the transactions and the closing position of the Stock Adjustment Account of his railway. This statement of the Stock Adjustment Account is annexed to the:
e: The statement of the Stock Adjustment Account, showing its transactions and closing position, is annexed to the Appropriation Accounts of the railway.

q: A scrap lot is knocked down in an e-auction and the purchaser deposits the earnest money and a part of the sale value. Under the conditions of sale, the balance of the sale value is payable by him within:
e: Under the conditions of sale of scrap, after earnest money and part payment, the balance of the sale value of an e-auction lot is payable within 40 days.

q: An enquiry into the conduct of a registered firm supplying stores is in progress, and, pending its completion, dealings with the firm are held up as a temporary step. Such suspension of business dealings with a firm, as distinct from banning it, is:

options.A: A permanent measure taken only after a full enquiry is completed
options.B: An interim measure adopted pending completion of the enquiry into the conduct of the firm
options.C: A measure applicable only to foreign firms
options.D: A measure which can be taken only after the firm has first been banned

e: Suspension of business dealings is an interim, temporary measure taken pending completion of the enquiry into a firm's conduct, unlike banning, which is imposed after the enquiry.

q: Before an order banning business dealings with a firm for supply of stores is issued against it, the firm is ordinarily:

options.A: Given an opportunity to show cause and explain its position
options.B: Required to deposit the full value of all its pending orders in cash
options.C: Struck off the list of registered firms without any notice to it
options.D: Debarred automatically from tenders for one year, without any order

e: Before business dealings with a firm are banned, principles of natural justice require that the firm is ordinarily given an opportunity to show cause and explain its position.

q: A purchase order for stores prescribes pre-despatch inspection, and the inspection is to be carried out by an agency acting on behalf of the Railways. Such inspection of purchased stores, where so prescribed, may be carried out by:

options.A: The Accounts stock verifiers of the railway
options.B: The supplier's own staff, without any independent check
options.C: RITES, acting as an inspection agency

e: Pre-despatch inspection of purchased stores, where prescribed, may be carried out by RITES acting as an inspection agency on behalf of the Railways.

q: A depot has to procure an item which is notified as a safety/critical item for train operation. Procurement of such an item can be made only from sources approved by:
e: Safety and critical items for train operation can be procured only from sources approved by RDSO, which approves vendors for such items.

q: A workshop is examining a stores item which performs its required function satisfactorily, but a cheaper design is available which performs the same function equally well without impairing quality or utility. The technique of examining the function performed by the item and eliminating its unnecessary cost in this manner is known as:
e: Value Analysis examines the function of an item and eliminates unnecessary cost where a cheaper design performs the same function equally well without impairing quality or utility.

q: In a railway stores depot, the book balance of every item is maintained continuously in the priced records as receipts and issues take place, and these balances are physically verified in rotation during the year. This system of inventory followed for railway stores accounts is the:

options.A: Periodic inventory system, under which stock is counted only at the end of the year
options.B: Bin card system, under which no priced records are maintained
options.C: Annual stock-taking system, dispensing with priced ledgers

e: Railway stores follow the perpetual inventory system: priced records show balances continuously with every receipt and issue, and balances are physically verified in rotation during the year.

q: A work returns a quantity of serviceable stores, earlier issued to it, to the depot. On examination, the stores are found fit for re-use but their present worth is less than the price at which they were originally issued. The credit to be given to the returning work for these stores is at:

options.A: The value assessed for the returned material
options.B: The price at which the stores were originally issued, in all cases
options.C: The current market price of new material of the same description
options.D: Nil, as no credit is given for stores returned to a depot

e: Serviceable stores returned to depot are credited to the returning work at the value assessed for the returned material, since their present worth may be less than the original issue price.

q:
Consider the following statements about a loss of stores noticed in a depot:
1. The loss can be written off straightaway by the storekeeper, without any enquiry, as soon as it is noticed.
2. Before the loss is written off, the responsibility for it is investigated and fixed, and recovery is made from the official at fault where negligence is established.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 2 only is correct: a loss cannot be written off without enquiry; responsibility is investigated and fixed first, and recovery is made from the official at fault where negligence is established.

q: The programme of stock verification in a stores depot is so drawn up by the Accounts Department that:

options.A: Every item held in the depot is physically verified at least once in a year
options.B: All the items of the depot are verified on one single day of the year
options.C: Only items costing above Rs 1 lakh are verified during the year
options.D: Each item is verified once in five years

e: The stock verification programme drawn up by Accounts ensures every item held in a depot is physically verified at least once in a year, in rotation.

q: A consignment received at a depot is opened in the presence of the carrier's representative and a part of the material is found short and another part damaged in transit. The correct course for the depot in such a case is to:

options.A: Accept the consignment silently and ignore the shortage and damage
options.B: Recover the value personally from the storekeeper, without any record
options.C: Record the shortage/damage on the receipt documents and prefer a claim on the supplier or the carrier, as the case may be
options.D: Deduct the amount from the next bill of the firm, without any record

e: Shortage or damage found on opening a consignment in the carrier's presence must be recorded on the receipt documents and a claim preferred on the supplier or carrier, as applicable.

q: Material despatched by a supplier has reached a depot and is lying there, but its inspection has not yet been completed and no receipt note has been issued for it. In the priced stock accounts of the depot, this material is taken into stock:

options.A: Immediately on its arrival at the depot gate
options.B: As soon as it is issued to a consuming department
options.C: At the end of the financial year, with the annual stock-taking
options.D: Only after it has been inspected and accepted and a receipt note issued

e: Material is taken into priced stock only after it has been inspected and accepted and a receipt note issued; mere arrival at the depot does not bring it on stock.

q: One depot of a railway despatches stores to another depot under a transfer order. Until the receiving depot acknowledges the receipt of the material, the stores so despatched remain accounted for:

options.A: In the books of the receiving depot, from the date of despatch
options.B: In no depot's books, the accounts being closed on despatch
options.C: In the books of the despatching depot
options.D: In the personal account of the storekeeper of the receiving depot

e: Until the receiving depot acknowledges receipt, stores despatched under a transfer order remain accounted for in the books of the despatching depot.

q: Under the periodic review (periodic ordering) system of inventory control followed for a stock item:

options.A: Stock is reviewed at fixed intervals and an order is placed to restore the stock to a predetermined target level
options.B: A fixed quantity is ordered whenever the stock falls to the re-order level
options.C: Orders are placed only when the stock is completely exhausted
options.D: The supplier himself reviews the stock and despatches material automatically

e: Under the periodic review system, stock is reviewed at fixed intervals and an order is placed to restore stock to a predetermined target level, unlike the fixed-quantity re-order level system.

q: Stores are purchased against a specific demand of a work, are received at the depot and are passed on to the work without being stocked as regular depot stock. Such non-stock stores are accounted for by:

options.A: Taking them into the priced stock of the depot like stock items
options.B: Crediting their value to Purchase Suspense
options.C: Including them in the closing balance of stores of the railway
options.D: Charging their cost direct to the work or department concerned, without routing them through the stock accounts

e: Non-stock stores bought for a specific work are charged direct to that work or department and are not routed through stock accounts or included in the closing stock balance.

q: Against a purchase order for 1,000 units of an item, a supplier delivers 650 units, which are received, inspected and accepted at the depot; the balance quantity is still awaited. The supplier's bill for the supply made is passed for payment:

options.A: For the full quantity of 1,000 units ordered, as the order is a concluded contract
options.B: Only for the quantity of 650 units actually received and accepted
options.C: For 98 per cent of the value of the full order, in all cases
options.D: Only after the entire quantity ordered has been received at the depot

e: A supplier's bill is passed only for the quantity actually received, inspected and accepted, here 650 units, not for the full 1,000 units ordered.

q: A firm supplies stores which do not fully conform to the specification in the purchase order, but the stores are usable for the intended purpose and the deviation is not material. Such stores may be accepted:

options.A: By the competent authority under a deviation, with a suitable reduction in price
options.B: By the depot storekeeper at the full contract price
options.C: Only if the supplier agrees to replace them during the warranty period
options.D: In no circumstances; such stores must always be rejected outright

e: Stores deviating from specification but usable, where the deviation is not material, may be accepted by the competent authority under a deviation with a suitable reduction in price.

q:
Consider the following statements about the pricing of stores issues in the priced accounts:
1. Each issue is valued at the purchase rate of the oldest lot held in stock, following the first-in-first-out method.
2. Issues are valued at the prevailing (average) book rate of the item, irrespective of the lot from which the material is physically drawn.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 2 only is correct: issues are priced at the prevailing average book rate of the item, not at the FIFO purchase rate of the oldest lot, though physical issue follows oldest stock first.

q:
Consider the following statements about the pricing of stores moving out of a depot:
1. Stores transferred from one depot to another depot of the same railway are priced at the book rate, without addition of departmental charges.
2. Stores issued to outside parties and other Government departments are priced at the book rate plus the prescribed departmental charges.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: transfers between depots of the same railway are at book rate without departmental charges, while issues to outside parties and other departments carry book rate plus departmental charges.

q: A purchase officer has to explain to a trainee how the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) differs from IREPS in railway procurement. The correct position is that:

options.A: GeM and IREPS are two names of one and the same portal
options.B: GeM is used by the Railways only for the sale of scrap
options.C: IREPS is the national marketplace for common-use goods and services
options.D: IREPS is the Railways' own e-procurement system for tenders, stores procurement and scrap e-auction, whereas GeM is the national marketplace for common-use goods and services

e: IREPS is the Railways' own e-procurement system for tenders, stores procurement and scrap e-auction, whereas GeM is the national marketplace for common-use goods and services.

q: Bills for stores purchased through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) portal are processed through the portal itself, and the portal is linked for this purpose with the Railways':
e: GeM bills are processed through the GeM portal, which is linked with the Railways' IPAS accounting system for payment purposes.

q: An accounts officer has to certify, at the half-year mark, that the balances shown by the priced stores ledger of his railway agree with the balances in the general books. The half-yearly Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts prepared for this purpose is:

options.A: A statement showing the balances of stores under the stock and suspense heads and proving the agreement of the priced ledger with the general books
options.B: A statement of the attendance of stores staff for the six months
options.C: A list of the tenders opened in the depots during the half year
options.D: A statement of the dues recoverable from stores staff

e: The half-yearly Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts shows balances under stock and suspense heads and proves agreement of the priced stores ledger with the general books.

q: For working out the cost of holding stores, a finance officer has to state how the inventory carrying cost of a railway is ordinarily expressed. It is ordinarily expressed as:

options.A: A fixed amount per depot, irrespective of the stock held
options.B: A proportion (percentage) of the average value of the inventory held, per annum
options.C: A flat charge per item held, irrespective of its value
options.D: A percentage of the salary bill of the stores department

e: Inventory carrying cost is ordinarily expressed as a percentage of the average value of inventory held, per annum, covering interest, storage and obsolescence costs of holding stock.

q: The buffer (safety) stock norms for A-category items of stores are kept comparatively tight, with only a low margin above the expected consumption during the lead time. This is mainly because:

options.A: A-category items are consumed only once in many years
options.B: A-category items are never required in an emergency
options.C: A large amount of capital is locked up in every unit of A-category stock, so an excess buffer is costly
options.D: A-category items are always available off the shelf in the market

e: Buffer norms for A-category items are kept tight because each unit locks up a large amount of capital, so an excess buffer over lead-time consumption is costly to hold.

q: A depot officer reporting on the stock position of an item states its 'coverage' as four months. In stores parlance, the coverage of a stock item means:

options.A: The quantity ordered in a single purchase order for the item
options.B: The shelf life of the item in the depot
options.C: The validity period of the tender under which the item is purchased
options.D: The period for which the stock in hand and on order (dues) will meet the consumption requirements of the item

e: Coverage means the period for which stock in hand plus dues on order will meet consumption requirements of the item, expressed in months of AAC.

q:
Consider the following statements about A-category items under ABC analysis of stores:
1. A-category items are comparatively few in number but account for the bulk of the annual consumption value.
2. A-category items are reviewed less frequently than C-category items.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 only is correct: A-category items are few in number but account for the bulk of annual consumption value, and they are in fact reviewed more, not less, frequently than C items.

q: Stores are imported from a foreign supplier against a Letter of Credit opened by the Railway through a bank. Under this arrangement, payment to the foreign supplier is made:

options.A: Only after the material has been received and verified in the Indian depot
options.B: In cash to the supplier's agent at the Indian port of entry
options.C: Only after the close of the financial year in which the order was placed
options.D: Against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents through the bank, and not on the physical receipt of the material in India

e: Under a Letter of Credit, the foreign supplier is paid through the bank against presentation of the stipulated shipping documents, not on physical receipt of material in India.

q: Stores supplied by a firm are found defective within the warranty period, a warranty claim is lodged in time, but the supplier fails to replace or repair the defective stores. In such a case, the Railway may:

options.A: Bear the cost of repair itself, as it has no remedy against the supplier
options.B: Drop the claim and throw away the defective stores
options.C: Arrange the repair or replacement at the supplier's risk and cost and recover the amount from his dues or security deposit
options.D: Ask the depot storekeeper to impose a fine on the supplier

e: If a supplier fails to repair or replace defective stores under a warranty claim lodged in time, the Railway may do so at his risk and cost and recover from his dues or security deposit.

q: Liquidated damages levied on a supplier for delayed supply of stores under a contract are ordinarily recovered from:

options.A: The supplier's bills or his security deposit with the Railway
options.B: The pay of the depot storekeeper who received the stores
options.C: The earnest money of the purchasers in the next scrap auction
options.D: No recovery is made, as liquidated damages are always waived

e: Liquidated damages for delayed supply are ordinarily recovered from the supplier's bills or his security deposit held by the Railway.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Stores Budget of a railway:
1. The 'debits' anticipated in the budget represent the value of stores expected to be purchased and received during the year.
2. The 'credits' anticipated in the budget represent the value of stores expected to be issued and sold during the year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: Stores Budget debits represent stores expected to be purchased and received, and credits represent stores expected to be issued and sold during the year.

q: A field official holding imprest stores has consumed a part of them on day-to-day requirements and renders an account of the consumption to the depot. His imprest stores are replenished by the depot on the basis of:

options.A: A fresh tender invited for every replenishment
options.B: The account of consumption rendered by the imprest holder
options.C: The annual budget allotment of the depot alone
options.D: A narrative report of the stock verifier

e: Imprest stores are replenished by the depot on the basis of the account of consumption rendered by the imprest holder, restoring the imprest to its fixed level.

q: During stock verification of a depot, the stock verifier finds a quantity of an item physically in excess of its book balance. The correct course in respect of this excess is that:

options.A: No stock sheet is prepared, as stock sheets are prepared only for shortages
options.B: The excess quantity is removed from the depot without any entry
options.C: The excess is treated as the personal property of the storekeeper
options.D: A stock sheet is prepared for the excess as for a shortage, and the excess is taken on stock with adjustment through the Stock Adjustment Account, after approval of the competent authority

e: A stock sheet is prepared for an excess as for a shortage, and the excess is taken on stock through the Stock Adjustment Account after approval of the competent authority.

q: During stock verification of a depot, the Assistant Stock Verifier notices several procedural irregularities in the maintenance of the depot records, apart from the physical balances themselves. These procedural irregularities are brought out by him through:

options.A: An error sheet issued to the depot
options.D: A muster roll of the depot staff

e: Procedural irregularities in depot records noticed during verification, apart from physical balances, are brought out by the Assistant Stock Verifier through a narrative report.

q: A quantity of stores in a depot has become unserviceable and is proposed to be condemned and surveyed off so that it can be disposed of. Such unserviceable stores are condemned and surveyed off on the recommendation of a:
e: Unserviceable stores are condemned and surveyed off on the recommendation of a Survey Committee, which examines and recommends disposal of such stores.

q: A depot finds that a quantity of serviceable stores held by it is surplus to its own requirements. Before such surplus stores are disposed of, the correct course is that they are:

options.A: Sold immediately by auction by the depot itself
options.B: Returned to the original supplier at the purchase price
options.C: Circulated and offered to other depots and railways which may require them
options.D: Written off from the books as dead stores

e: Serviceable surplus stores are first circulated and offered to other depots and railways that may need them; only if not required elsewhere are they disposed of.

q: In the FSN analysis of a depot's inventory, an item which has had no issue or movement at all for a long period is classified as a:
e: In FSN analysis, an item with no issue or movement for a long period is a non-moving item, as distinct from fast-moving and slow-moving items.

q: The Turnover Ratio of the stores of a railway for a year works out to 0.40. This means that the closing stock held in the depots of the railway is broadly equivalent to:
e: A Turnover Ratio of 0.40 means closing stock is 0.40 of a year's issues, equal to 0.40 x 12 = 4.8 months' issues held in stock.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A credit balance under Purchase Suspense represents material which has been received at depots but for which the suppliers' bills have not yet been paid.
2. A debit balance under Sales Suspense represents sale value which has been deposited by a purchaser but against which the material has not yet been delivered to him.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: a credit balance under Purchase Suspense means material received but suppliers' bills unpaid. Statement 2 is wrong: sale value deposited against material not yet delivered is a credit balance under Sales Suspense, so only statement 1 is correct.

q: The opening debit balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is Rs 6 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 26 lakh are paid, and material worth Rs 29 lakh is received at the depots and linked with the bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense is:

options.A: A debit balance of Rs 9 lakh
options.B: A credit balance of Rs 3 lakh
options.C: A debit balance of Rs 3 lakh
options.D: A debit balance of Rs 6 lakh

e: Closing Purchase Suspense debit equals opening debit plus bills paid minus material received and linked: 6 + 26 - 29 = Rs 3 lakh debit.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 7,200 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 200 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 8 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity of the item is:
e: EOQ equals square root of (2 x annual consumption x ordering cost / carrying cost) = square root of (2 x 7200 x 200 / 8) = square root of 3,60,000 = 600 units.

q: A depot holds 700 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 22 per unit. A fresh receipt of 300 units is taken into stock at Rs 37 per unit. The revised book (average) rate of the item after the fresh receipt will be:
The AAC of an item is 10,800 units. The stock in hand is 1,350 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 450 units. The coverage available for the item is:
e: Monthly consumption is 10,800 / 12 = 900 units. Coverage equals (1350 + 450) / 900 = 1800 / 900 = 2 months.

q: The average consumption of an item is 90 units per week, the lead time for its procurement is 7 weeks and the safety (buffer) stock provided for it is 270 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level equals consumption during lead time plus safety stock: 90 x 7 + 270 = 630 + 270 = 900 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,750 units and the re-order quantity is 1,250 units. The minimum consumption is 55 units per week and the minimum lead time is 5 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum level equals re-order level plus re-order quantity minus minimum consumption during minimum lead time: 1750 + 1250 - (55 x 5) = 3000 - 275 = 2725 units.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,320 units. The average consumption is 95 units per week and the average lead time is 6 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:
e: Minimum level equals re-order level minus average consumption during average lead time: 1320 - (95 x 6) = 1320 - 570 = 750 units.

q: The maximum consumption of an item is 210 units per week, its normal consumption is 160 units per week and the lead time for its procurement is 4 weeks. The safety (buffer) stock to be provided for the item is:
e: Safety stock equals (maximum minus normal consumption) x lead time: (210 - 160) x 4 = 50 x 4 = 200 units, covering the excess demand during the lead time.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 4,20,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 6 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week of delay amount to:
e: LD is 0.5 per cent of Rs 4,20,000 = Rs 2,100 per week. For 6 weeks of delay, LD = 2100 x 6 = Rs 12,600 under the liquidated damages clause.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 7,75,000. The advance payment admissible at 98 per cent of the bill value, against the inspection certificate and despatch documents, is:
e: Advance payment at 98 per cent of Rs 7,75,000 = Rs 7,59,500, admissible against inspection certificate and despatch documents before material reaches destination.

q: During stock verification of a depot, a shortage of 22 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 475 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Shortage value equals quantity short x book rate: 22 x Rs 475 = Rs 10,450, accounted for through a stock sheet and the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: During stock verification of a depot, 18 units of an item are found physically in excess of the book balance. The book rate of the item is Rs 325 per unit. The value of the excess taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account is:
e: Excess value equals quantity in excess x book rate: 18 x Rs 325 = Rs 5,850, taken into stock through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: A depot holds 950 units of an item whose book rate is revised from Rs 88 to Rs 79 per unit. The decrease in the value of the stock in hand, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account, is:
e: Decrease in stock value equals quantity x fall in rate: 950 x (88 - 79) = 950 x 9 = Rs 8,550, adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q: While framing the Stores Budget of a railway, the budget officer notices that the value of stores to be drawn for works and maintenance programmes is also reflected in the estimates of the consuming departments. To ensure that the same requirement is not provided for twice in the budget, the Stores Budget provides for:

options.B: An appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.C: A charge to the Stock Adjustment Account

e: The Stores Budget uses a deduct entry to avoid double provision, since stores drawn for works and maintenance are already reflected in the estimates of the consuming departments.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Stores Monthly Summary prepared by a depot forms the basis for compilation of the stores accounts of the railway.
2. The half-yearly Balance Sheet of Stores Accounts proves the agreement of the priced ledger balances with the balances in the general books.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the depot Stores Monthly Summary is the basis for compiling the railway's stores accounts, and the half-yearly Balance Sheet proves priced ledger balances against the general books.

q: A stock item held in a depot is in serviceable condition and was issued regularly until recently, but the class of equipment for which it was stocked has been withdrawn and replaced by a new design, so that the item can no longer be put to use. Such stores are correctly described as:
e: Stores that are serviceable but can no longer be used because the equipment they served has been withdrawn and replaced are obsolete stores, not scrap or dead surplus.

q: A supplier has despatched stores against a purchase order and furnished the inspection certificate and despatch documents, against which advance payment of 98 per cent of the bill value has been made to him, the material itself being still in transit. Pending receipt of the material at the destination depot, this advance payment is held under:
e: Advance payment of 98 per cent made against inspection certificate and despatch documents, while material is still in transit, is held under Purchase Suspense pending receipt and linking at destination.

q: A Section Engineer of a consuming department wishes to ascertain the stock of an item available in the depots of his railway and to raise his demand for it online, without visiting the depot. The facility provided to him for this purpose is the:
e: The user depot module of iMMS lets consuming department officials check depot stock availability and raise their demands online without visiting the depot.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Issues of stores from a depot are ordinarily made on the first-in-first-out basis, the oldest stock being issued first, so as to prevent deterioration and obsolescence.
2. Every issue of stores is priced at the prevailing book (average) rate of the item and not at the purchase rate of the particular lot from which the material is physically drawn.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: physical issues follow first-in-first-out so oldest stock goes first, and every issue is priced at the prevailing average book rate, not the lot purchase rate.

q: Stores supplied against a purchase made through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) have been received by the consignee. Before payment to the seller can be processed on the portal, the consignee is required to generate the:
e: On GeM, after receipt of stores the consignee must generate the Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate (CRAC) before payment to the seller can be processed on the portal.

q: An inventory analyst groups the stores items of a depot according to whether they are obtained from Government sources, from ordinary trade sources, from local sources or from foreign sources. The analysis being carried out by him is:
e: Grouping items by source of supply - Government, Ordinary trade, Local and Foreign - is GOLF analysis, from the initial letters of the four sources.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A tenderer who withdraws his tender during the period of validity of his offer is liable to forfeit his earnest money deposit.
2. A tenderer who is asked to extend the validity of his offer after its expiry may refuse to do so without forfeiting his earnest money.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: withdrawing a tender during its validity forfeits earnest money, but a tenderer asked to extend validity after expiry may refuse without forfeiting earnest money.

q: A stores depot issues 250 units of an item, whose book rate is Rs 96 per unit, to an outside party. Departmental charges are leviable at 12.5 per cent of the book value. The total amount recoverable from the party is:
e: Book value is 250 x 96 = Rs 24,000. Departmental charges at 12.5 per cent are Rs 3,000, so total recoverable from the outside party is 24,000 + 3,000 = Rs 27,000.

q: A purchase order is placed for stores valued at Rs 4,80,000. The security deposit prescribed under the contract at 10 per cent of the order value works out to:
e: Security deposit at 10 per cent of the order value of Rs 4,80,000 = Rs 48,000, as prescribed under the stores contract conditions.

q: Six wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for 4 days beyond the free time allowed for unloading them. Demurrage is payable at Rs 1,100 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Demurrage equals wagons x days x rate: 6 x 4 x Rs 1,100 = Rs 26,400 for detention beyond free time.

q: A depot holds on an average 6,500 units of an item whose book rate is Rs 120 per unit. The inventory carrying cost is estimated at 18 per cent per annum of the value of the stock held. The annual inventory carrying cost of the item is:
e: Average stock value is 6500 x Rs 120 = Rs 7,80,000. Carrying cost at 18 per cent = Rs 1,40,400 per annum.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 5,400 units and orders for it are placed in Economic Order Quantities of 600 units each. If the cost of placing one order is Rs 250, the total ordering cost incurred during the year is:
e: Number of orders equals 5400 / 600 = 9. Total ordering cost is 9 x Rs 250 = Rs 2,250 for the year.

q: The annual requirement of an item is 8,640 units and the quantity ordered each time is 540 units. The number of orders placed for the item during the year is:
e: Number of orders equals annual requirement divided by quantity per order: 8640 / 540 = 16 orders in the year.

q:
Consider the following statements about local suppliers under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order:
1. A supplier whose local content is at least 20 per cent but less than 50 per cent is a Class-II local supplier.
2. A supplier whose local content is less than 20 per cent is treated as a non-local supplier.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct under the Make in India Order: local content of 20 per cent to less than 50 per cent makes a Class-II local supplier, and below 20 per cent the supplier is non-local.

q: In a stores tender, the lowest bid (L1) is Rs 2,00,000. A Micro and Small Enterprise has quoted Rs 2,24,000, which is within the price band of L1 plus 15 per cent. Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, the enterprise may be allowed to:

options.A: Supply the entire order at its own quoted price of Rs 2,24,000
options.B: Claim exemption from furnishing any security deposit
options.C: Reject the L1 price and fix its own terms of supply
options.D: Supply up to 25 per cent of the total order quantity, provided it matches the L1 price

e: An MSE quoting within L1 plus 15 per cent may be allowed to supply up to 25 per cent of the total order quantity, provided it matches the L1 price, under the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs.

q: Grave allegations of malpractice have been received against a registered firm supplying stores, and an enquiry into its conduct has been ordered but is yet to be completed. Pending completion of the enquiry, the interim measure that may be taken against the firm is:

options.A: Suspension of business dealings with the firm
options.C: Cancellation of all purchase orders already placed on other firms
options.D: Imposition of a fine by the depot storekeeper

e: Pending completion of an enquiry into a firm's conduct, the interim measure is suspension of business dealings with the firm; banning follows only after the enquiry.

q: A stores depot issues material to a railway workshop specifically for use on the periodical overhaul (POH) of rolling stock undertaken in the workshop. The value of such stores is classified under:
e: Stores issued to a workshop for periodical overhaul (POH) of rolling stock are classified under Primary Unit 35, which covers workshop and POH-related stores consumption.

q: Material drawn from a stores depot is delivered to a railway workshop for use on a job of manufacture being executed there. Until the job is completed and its cost is adjusted, the value of the material, together with the labour and on-cost booked on the job, is initially held under:
e: Material, labour and on-cost booked on a workshop manufacture job are held under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense until the job is completed and its cost adjusted.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 68 lakh, receipts of stores during the year are Rs 1.72 crore and issues during the year are Rs 1.58 crore. The closing balance of stores of the railway is:
e: Closing balance equals opening plus receipts minus issues: 68 + 172 - 158 = Rs 82 lakh.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 1.35 crore and the closing balance is Rs 95 lakh. The average stock held by the railway during the year is:
e: Average stock equals (opening balance plus closing balance) / 2 = (135 + 95) / 2 = Rs 115 lakh = Rs 1.15 crore.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 1.26 crore and the total issues of stores during the year are Rs 8.4 crore. The Turnover Ratio of the stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio equals closing balance divided by total issues: Rs 1.26 crore / Rs 8.4 crore = 0.15.

q: A supplier fails to supply 650 units of stores contracted at Rs 64 per unit. A risk purchase of the same quantity is made at Rs 81 per unit. The extra cost recoverable from the defaulting supplier is:
e: Risk purchase extra cost equals (risk rate minus contract rate) x quantity: (81 - 64) x 650 = 17 x 650 = Rs 11,050, recoverable from the defaulting supplier.

q: A purchaser of a scrap lot delays lifting the material for 9 days beyond the delivery period allowed to him. Ground rent is leviable at Rs 550 per day for the period of delay, as per the conditions of sale. The ground rent payable by him is:
e: Ground rent equals days of delay x daily rate: 9 x Rs 550 = Rs 4,950 under the conditions of sale.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. High-value 'A' category items held in a stores depot are physically verified twice a year.
2. Besides the programmed periodical verification, Accounts stock verifiers may carry out surprise checks of stores balances without prior intimation to the custodian.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: high-value A-category items are physically verified twice a year, and Accounts stock verifiers may also make surprise checks without prior intimation to the custodian.

q: An inventory review finds that a particular stores item is both in the highest annual-consumption-value class under ABC analysis and classed as vital in use under VED analysis. The control appropriate for such an item is:

options.A: The loosest control, with bulk purchase for long periods
options.B: The strictest inventory control, with a close watch on its stock levels and consumption
options.C: No stocking of the item at all
options.D: Its immediate declaration as surplus stores

e: An item that is both A-category by consumption value and vital in use needs the strictest inventory control, with a close watch on stock levels and consumption to avoid both stock-out and excess capital lock-up.

q: A purchase office places an order on a firm for the supply of a specified definite quantity of 5,000 units of an item at the contracted rate, the whole quantity being committed in the order itself. The arrangement so made is a:
e: An order committing a specified definite quantity, here 5,000 units, at the contracted rate is a definite quantity contract, unlike a rate contract under which quantities are ordered as required.

q: A consignment of purchased stores has physically arrived at a stores depot and is lying in the receipt section awaiting inspection. At this stage, the correct accounting treatment of the consignment is that it is:

options.A: Taken into the priced stock accounts immediately on arrival at the depot gate
options.B: Issued to the consuming department and charged to it at once
options.C: Treated as stock in hand for all purposes, including stock verification
options.D: Taken into the priced stock accounts only after it has been inspected and accepted and a receipt note has been issued for it

e: A consignment awaiting inspection is taken into priced stock only after it has been inspected and accepted and a receipt note issued, not on mere arrival at the depot.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 10,000 units and it is ordered in Economic Order Quantities of 500 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 125 and the inventory carrying cost is Rs 5 per unit per year. The total of the annual ordering cost and the annual carrying cost of the item is:
e: Ordering cost is (10,000 / 500) x 125 = Rs 2,500; carrying cost is (500 / 2) x 5 = Rs 1,250. Total annual cost is 2500 + 1250 = Rs 3,750 at the EOQ.

q: The opening balance under Purchase Suspense of a railway is a credit balance of Rs 7 lakh. During the month, stores bills amounting to Rs 42 lakh are paid, while material worth Rs 38 lakh is received at the depots and linked with bills. The closing balance under Purchase Suspense will be:

options.A: A debit balance of Rs 11 lakh
options.B: A debit balance of Rs 3 lakh
options.C: A credit balance of Rs 3 lakh
options.D: A credit balance of Rs 11 lakh

e: Opening credit of Rs 7 lakh is minus 7 in debit terms. Closing equals -7 + bills paid 42 - material received 38 = minus Rs 3 lakh, that is a credit balance of Rs 3 lakh under Purchase Suspense.

q: A depot holds 400 units of an item at a book rate of Rs 75 per unit. A fresh receipt of 600 units is taken into stock at Rs 95 per unit. The revised book (average) rate at which issues will thereafter be made is:
e: Revised average rate equals (400 x 75 + 600 x 95) / 1000 = (30,000 + 57,000) / 1000 = Rs 87 per unit, at which later issues are priced.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 45 lakh and the total issues of stores during the year are Rs 225 lakh. The Turnover Ratio of stores of the railway is:
e: Turnover Ratio equals closing balance divided by total issues: 45 / 225 = 0.20.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 60 lakh. The Stores Budget anticipates debits (purchases and receipts) of Rs 240 lakh and credits (issues and sales) of Rs 255 lakh during the year. The closing balance of stores anticipated at the end of the year is:
e: Anticipated closing balance equals opening plus debits minus credits: 60 + 240 - 255 = Rs 45 lakh, as projected in the Stores Budget.

q: Against an inspection certificate and despatch documents, advance payment is claimed by a supplier on stores valued at Rs 3,75,000. The advance payment that can be made to him, at the prescribed percentage of the value, is:
e: Advance payment at the prescribed 98 per cent of Rs 3,75,000 = Rs 3,67,500, against inspection certificate and despatch documents.

q: The value of a stores contract is Rs 45 lakh. Supplies under the contract are delayed. The maximum liquidated damages recoverable under the contract, at the prescribed ceiling, is:
e: Maximum LD is capped at 10 per cent of contract value: 10 per cent of Rs 45 lakh = Rs 4,50,000, whatever the period of delay.

q: Stores of the value of Rs 6,00,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied four weeks late. Liquidated damages are leviable at 0.5 per cent of the value of the stores in arrear for each week or part of a week of delay. The liquidated damages recoverable are:
e: LD is 0.5 per cent of Rs 6,00,000 = Rs 3,000 per week. For 4 weeks, LD = 3000 x 4 = Rs 12,000.

q: For a stores tender, a tender notice stipulates an Earnest Money Deposit of Rs 80 lakh, the tender being of very high value. A tenderer objects that the amount stipulated exceeds the maximum ceiling prescribed for Earnest Money Deposit in stores tenders. The ceiling he relies on is:
e: Earnest Money Deposit in stores tenders is subject to a ceiling of Rs 50 lakh, so a stipulation of Rs 80 lakh exceeds the prescribed maximum.

q: A purchaser of scrap lifts the material ten days after the expiry of the delivery period allowed to him. Ground rent is leviable at Rs 300 per day for the period of delay in lifting. The ground rent payable by him is:
e: Ground rent equals days of delayed lifting x daily rate: 10 x Rs 300 = Rs 3,000.

q: Seven wagons loaded with stores are detained at a depot for three days beyond the free time allowed for unloading them. Demurrage is payable at Rs 1,000 per wagon per day. The total demurrage payable is:
e: Demurrage equals wagons x days x rate: 7 x 3 x Rs 1,000 = Rs 21,000 for detention beyond free time.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 96 lakh. The inventory carrying cost is estimated, as given, at 12.5 per cent per annum of the average stock value. The annual inventory carrying cost borne by the railway is:
e: Annual inventory carrying cost equals 12.5 per cent of average stock value Rs 96 lakh = Rs 12 lakh.

q: The Average Annual Consumption of an item is 9,600 units and coverage for five months is to be provided. The stock in hand is 1,300 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 900 units. The quantity to be ordered is:
e: Quantity for 5 months is 9600 / 12 x 5 = 4000 units. Less stock 1300 and dues 900, the quantity to be ordered is 4000 - 2200 = 1800 units.

q: The average consumption of a stock item is 25 units per day, its lead time is 20 days and its safety (buffer) stock is 300 units. The re-order level of the item is:
e: Re-order level equals consumption during lead time plus safety stock: 25 x 20 + 300 = 500 + 300 = 800 units.

q: The average consumption of a stock item is 60 units per day and the lead time for its emergency procurement is, as given, 5 days. The danger level of the item is:
e: Danger level equals average consumption x emergency procurement lead time: 60 x 5 = 300 units, at which urgent procurement action is triggered.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,500 units and its re-order quantity is 1,000 units. Its minimum consumption is 50 units per week and the minimum lead time is 6 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:
e: Maximum level equals re-order level plus re-order quantity minus minimum consumption during minimum lead time: 1500 + 1000 - (50 x 6) = 2500 - 300 = 2200 units.
